mcqs.q: Why does correlation not imply causation in geographical data?
options: Savanna trees are scattered because lions eat too many of them.
Correlation and causation are the same thing.
If two variables correlate strongly, one must cause the other.
Two variables may correlate because of a third confounding factor, coincidence, or reverse causation — statistical association alone does not prove one causes the other.

mcqs.q: What maintains the savanna biome's mix of grass and scattered trees?
options: Savanna trees are scattered because lions eat too many of them.
Correlation and causation are the same thing.
The savanna is dry because it's halfway between rainforest and desert.
A pronounced wet/dry season prevents continuous forest, frequent fires kill saplings, and large herbivores (e.g. elephants) suppress tree regeneration — maintaining open grass-dominated landscape.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between physical and economic water scarcity?
options: Correlation and causation are the same thing.
Economic scarcity means water is too expensive for governments to buy.
Water scarcity only happens in dry countries.

Physical scarcity is insufficient water supply for demand (e.g. arid regions); economic scarcity is inability to access available water due to lack of infrastructure or investment, despite water being present.
